summary: Post-market, the composite risk score eased 0.93 to 42.57, holding in caution within a goldilocks regime of low volatility and positive momentum, with breadth above its 200-day average at 69.03%. The day's session was risk-on: memory led all themes at 5.47% (Micron 5.04%), autos gained 3.44% (Tesla 3.44%), and AI software, cloud and fintech rose 3.17% to 4.09%, with the VIX falling to 14.55 from 15.28. The easing was macro-driven: headline CPI slowed to 3.3 and core to 2.47, prompting traders to unwind rate-hike bets even as Fed officials stay publicly split (Barkin hold vs Hammack hike). The key tension is narrow leadership: the new-highs ratio is only 10.32% and cross-asset confirmation dropped to 0.375, while AI-financing froth builds (AMD bond plans, NVIDIA data-center securitization reports). Tomorrow's Advance Retail Sales is the next macro test.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Macro remains the binding constraint: the 10-year real rate of 2.43 sits at the 99.04 percentile and the 10-year yield of 4.7 at the 98.15 percentile, keeping the macro dimension at 62.21.
The largest single contributor is the cross-asset confirmation proxy at 0.375, which added 7.5 to the composite — equity gains were not confirmed across other asset classes.
Leadership is narrow: 69.03% of stocks sit above their 200-day average, yet the new-highs ratio is just 10.32% — the rally is not broadening into new highs.
Liquidity support is thinning: the reverse-repo balance fell to 0.45 (risk score 95.51) and high-yield spreads are already tight at 2.71, leaving little cushion if risk sentiment turns.
Policy-path uncertainty persists: mild core CPI (2.47) unwound rate-hike bets (top-news importance 51.13), yet Fed officials remain publicly split between holding and hiking.

supporting_signals.claim: Disinflation is back on track: headline CPI slowed to 3.3 from 3.46 and core to 2.47 from 2.57, with 5-year breakevens easing to 2.28.
Volatility is the calmest dimension (score 21.71): the VIX fell to 14.55 from 15.28 and realized volatility to 13.98.
Rates eased across the curve: the 10-year yield slipped to 4.7 from 4.72 and the 2-year to 4.22 from 4.25, while high-yield OAS tightened to 2.71 from 2.72.
The rally was broad: memory led at 5.47% (Micron 5.04%), fintech rose 4.09%, autos 3.44% (Tesla 3.44%), cloud 3.36% and AI software 3.17% — 19 of 22 themes finished higher.

contradicting_signals.claim: Cross-asset confirmation sits at a muted 0.375, below the 0.5 neutral mark — the equity advance is not confirmed by other asset classes.
Despite the rally, only 10.32% of stocks printed new highs, data centers — the physical AI backbone — rose just 0.08%, and networking fell 1.39%.
AI-financing froth is building: AMD is reportedly planning a record investment-grade bond sale and NVIDIA is reportedly exploring data-center securitization — leverage is financing the AI build-out.

what_changed_today: The composite risk score eased 0.93 to 42.57 (caution/goldilocks); the one-week trend is -0.62.
Volatility and yields eased: the VIX fell to 14.55 from 15.28, the 10-year to 4.7 from 4.72 and the 2-year to 4.22 from 4.25.
Cross-asset confirmation dropped to 0.375 and the new-highs ratio held at just 10.32%.
Memory led the session at 5.47% (Micron 5.04%) while networking lagged at -1.39%.
Rate-hike bets unwound after a mild CPI print (headline 3.3, core 2.47), and Workday jumped about 18% on a Silver Lake takeover report before trading was halted.
watch_next: Advance Retail Sales (high importance) prints 08-14 — the consumer momentum test after CPI and PPI.
Watch whether the Fed's public split (Barkin hold vs Hammack hike) resolves before the next meeting.
Earnings queue: BIDU 08-18, TGT 08-19, BABA and WMT 08-20, ZM 08-25, then NVDA with PCE on 08-26.
Memory stays in focus: whether DRAM/HBM pricing keeps the supercycle bid alive or the cycle-top debate caps the 5.47% theme leader.

bull_case.title: Rates ease into disinflation
points: CPI (headline 3.3, core 2.47) and PPI confirm disinflation, unwinding rate-hike bets and easing policy risk.
Volatility is low (VIX 14.55) and credit calm (HY OAS 2.71), a permissive backdrop for risk assets.
Breadth of participation improved: memory 5.47%, fintech 4.09%, autos 3.44% and cloud 3.36% all advancing.

base_case.title: Goldilocks holds, macro is the ceiling
points: The composite at 42.57 stays in caution with a flat-to-down one-week trend of -0.62 — grinding higher rather than trending.
The real rate of 2.43 (99.04 percentile) and the 10-year yield of 4.7 (98.15 percentile) cap valuations.
Leadership stays narrow (new highs 10.32%) with cross-asset confirmation at 0.375 — gains need macro confirmation to extend.

bear_case.title: Macro and liquidity sting
points: The real rate at 2.43 (99.04 percentile) is the tightest macro constraint; a renewed yield backup would pressure the whole complex.
Liquidity support is thin: the reverse-repo balance of 0.45 leaves little dry powder, and labor cracks show in payrolls of -23.0.
AI-financing froth (AMD bond plans, NVIDIA securitization reports) plus narrow new-highs breadth of 10.32% could unwind quickly if sentiment turns.
